plan.title: Zebrafish larvae drug-exposure DE + human-ortholog pathway enrichment
plan.analytical_narrative: Design is a straightforward two-group unpaired comparison (3 treated vs 3 control zebrafish larvae pools, single batch, raw Salmon gene-level counts on Ensembl D. rerio annotation, ~12,000 genes x 6 samples). Track 1 runs the standard DESeq2 workflow grounded in the knowledge service's returned procedure: sample-structure QC (blind VST + PCA + sample-distance heatmap), a minimal low-count pre-filter (>=10 counts in >= the smallest group size of 3), median-of-ratios normalization inside the DESeq2 model, an explicit reference level (control) with the contrast named condition treated-vs-control, the DESeq2 Wald test with apeglm log2FC shrinkage, and BH-adjusted independent filtering at alpha=0.05. Because n=3/group gives low power (per rule R-0017/R-0094), the report states the expected-power caveat explicitly rather than loosening thresholds. Track 2 addresses pathway interpretation: zebrafish has no curated MSigDB/WikiPathways gene-set collection in this environment (only human, mouse, rat WikiPathways and MSigDB collections are staged; org.Dr.eg.db is present for zebrafish gene ID handling but not a pathway collection). Per rule R-0050, zebrafish gene symbols are mapped to their one-to-one human orthologs (via the babelgene package, which is installed) and the human Hallmark, Reactome, WikiPathways, and canonical-pathway (KEGG MEDICUS/BioCarta/PID) gene sets are used for a preranked fgsea analysis on the DESeq2 Wald statistic. The ortholog-mapping step and the share of genes lost to non-one-to-one orthology are reported explicitly as a stated limitation, not hidden. The final report step consolidates DE results, fit diagnostics, the power caveat, the ortholog-mapping caveat, and the enrichment tables with leading-edge genes.
